name: Cormac Abubakar-Yuen
creator: Cormac Abubakar-Yuen
description: The closest thing GLMZ has to a universally acknowledged living master, Abubakar-Yuen's six novels over thirty years constitute what critics call 'the long reckoning' — each book a generation-spanning examination of how ordinary people become complicit in systems they know to be wrong. His 2215 novel 'The Good Work' follows four generations of a Tier 2 family employed in corponation infrastructure maintenance, ending in the present day with a grandchild who services the systems her grandparents built without ever knowing what they were actually for. He writes by hand on paper, which is well known and frequently mythologized.
medium: physical hardprint primary; licensed neural feed editions produced by Aether Media with his reluctant approval
cultural_impact: Abubakar-Yuen is read in Tier 5 book circles and passed hand-to-hand in Tier 1. He occupies the rare position of being claimed by every tier as 'one of ours,' which he has said in the only interview he gives — one per decade — is both the thing he hoped for and the thing he finds most suspicious about his own work.
controversy: His refusal to allow deep-immersion neural editions of his work — only standard text-feed — has caused ongoing conflict with Aether Media, who hold his licensed distribution rights. A leaked contract clause suggests they have the right to produce immersive editions after his death, which he has publicly called 'a clause for corpse-mining.'
story_hooks: Abubakar-Yuen's handwritten manuscript for his seventh novel has been stolen — and its contents, if published, would ruin a Tier 5 family that has been quietly funding his work for years.
He is dying and has chosen to give his final interview to an unknown Shelf journalist — the choice is baffling to the literary establishment and the journalist needs help understanding why.
The 'good work' of infrastructure maintenance described in his novel turns out to have been covering for something — and a character's grandchild in real life has just found out what.
